Healthcare providers use it to screen for liver conditions, investigate symptoms like jaundice or abdominal pain, and monitor medication side effects or ongoing liver disease.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF1zvHy3I7EcDUXe8Gj6A2DvwxavsXjViDuasQDlHDxVMa4mqR8AQ3F9WQY9luGKtV14i80K4xX6syQpxJXKtH4H7sG3yfCq511khLrtKCc2lMWe9rthJ63-YIoHzQOpocfaHEjtESXyYNPpO1eoTc5SMUGCSbc6AV3U2Ko5fi4IdD4NR_UJIp61swq2I)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXQgjWZCrkhJPViVQcvG3TPKUXFh6fDv31rqP2smICHztDWXUs0zSKgGfmljIy9fEFGUChT6_D1WElnl-PYXepFnzMjPh8Z886_ejkCG0DBL5YS9UmtGGugPlOqYTZ2dbhrMXJ6ASEDZ1eZ6UcCiHp)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESowEBxCJF1_gmiVS2AN-SPrc10MQALdn7rTRBBCVZjd8F4Zx_XSwPm01FMwZtDr1owpeB7ju1dytyD1Jl01jj4ZryR7eBm8wpm9hor-I3Mi6YeetgHfmdvB-XPxkmAlsBTUWPJr5OQzhZKzn-HmmXTPhDCcKYe8Y89DJlIFrL9VfGMpIoSf8sA59n6Sn3g-wHzdC29FH1h7zptwtcV8giN_IoscZ6)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESngEBxCJF1xM_fzfX-WnVy20M6Fi2B1CvR5dr2J8dCwBDHLycthObt-wr3b9kxJpayj-J8W9qCvtnvVMUYgs4UNAeh6cok2p62WQamaONzBMVJ_nw8ICS4eov8rJhrSprk9SAhtGCqHgQ1hBJ57sQvCi5jWMW3fcP8GqodzxNT_n33eglf1OVMqpsJFenm0eaLkItrM1sMK3JQ1LJ1Le2aA)

### Common Tests in a Liver Panel

- **ALT (Alanine transaminase) & AST (Aspartate transaminase):** Enzymes released into the bloodstream when liver cells are stressed or injured. ALT is more specific to the liver, while AST is also found in muscle and other tissues.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXQgjWZCrkhJPViVQcvG3TPKUXFh6fDv31rqP2smICHztDWXUs0zSKgGfmljIy9fEFGUChT6_D1WElnl-PYXepFnzMjPh8Z886_ejkCG0DBL5YS9UmtGGugPlOqYTZ2dbhrMXJ6ASEDZ1eZ6UcCiHp)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiQEBxCJF15xsp2xkEhSIvpzntILRhlsMNltSarB3il487YF-leMKm4wmdRE7ekl20xfJ4SVeerEZogRTQ4H-SKBpGJ-46xvCK0gwIxNz3zYRxQ5CC-ktTQBQjasFj8cKLjVJ6zqms0kglZZAZPnyDkyBIV5y3If7Tq5Dse40mGqIQwc6jv7RrSS7PA)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESowEBxCJF1y_5_YQvrB4OGQRG3CFhgt-HcJxIfQP8KVxww0bWLEGkb7pCR7cNoA6uITVm7xnzBtU0nxyNMllujj5Wnzx3xJqG45EIZVqXTYMuCa4158CGYHLsmkKeFdxtLBf7M0UaJ9-KjWDQG69WLlCGjxpYzaTBwptF9ysc1T0SPnWAbwq8aBHIznr295NW6Kmzt4H5hlETEhstrro3AFQSKM2L)
- **ALP (Alkaline phosphatase) & GGT (Gamma-glutamyl transferase):** Enzymes linked to the liver and bile ducts. High levels can point to bile flow issues or bile duct inflammation (ALP is also found in bone).[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cu0H7L_cYQc&t=3)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXQgjWZCrkhJPViVQcvG3TPKUXFh6fDv31rqP2smICHztDWXUs0zSKgGfmljIy9fEFGUChT6_D1WElnl-PYXepFnzMjPh8Z886_ejkCG0DBL5YS9UmtGGugPlOqYTZ2dbhrMXJ6ASEDZ1eZ6UcCiHp)
- **Bilirubin:** A waste product from broken-down red blood cells that the liver processes and clears. High levels can cause yellowing of the skin and eyes (jaundice).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXQgjWZCrkhJPViVQcvG3TPKUXFh6fDv31rqP2smICHztDWXUs0zSKgGfmljIy9fEFGUChT6_D1WElnl-PYXepFnzMjPh8Z886_ejkCG0DBL5YS9UmtGGugPlOqYTZ2dbhrMXJ6ASEDZ1eZ6UcCiHp)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cu0H7L_cYQc&t=3)
- **Albumin & Total Protein:** Proteins made largely by the liver that help keep fluid in blood vessels and support overall body functions. Low albumin can signal reduced liver production, malnutrition, or other health issues.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESvgEBxCJF1xV8R5RxSgZNKyYKUPMj6_B4npSI0EsjoINqkTGVV-d4PKeYdSBiBI-vKt6vSUEr5xs8RPPK-IUlVO9sFi1i58n-ZGGfwuZ4J-IuTaPBowR2X4X2Hb79Oqc69i-QQ9L7SjzDs40IP7xFacK1ZNy2wXZN-JboikPSb1sJi2K0IMsfmwKf6h0OPa9i4HOomFl0A-YKY6ZWrdeL0yoKZJJKh58zLD-hVEQPLAWAniERkZCE806B2Cq9vIHo)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXQgjWZCrkhJPViVQcvG3TPKUXFh6fDv31rqP2smICHztDWXUs0zSKgGfmljIy9fEFGUChT6_D1WElnl-PYXepFnzMjPh8Z886_ejkCG0DBL5YS9UmtGGugPlOqYTZ2dbhrMXJ6ASEDZ1eZ6UcCiHp)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESowEBxCJF1_gmiVS2AN-SPrc10MQALdn7rTRBBCVZjd8F4Zx_XSwPm01FMwZtDr1owpeB7ju1dytyD1Jl01jj4ZryR7eBm8wpm9hor-I3Mi6YeetgHfmdvB-XPxkmAlsBTUWPJr5OQzhZKzn-HmmXTPhDCcKYe8Y89DJlIFrL9VfGMpIoSf8sA59n6Sn3g-wHzdC29FH1h7zptwtcV8giN_IoscZ6)[[4]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i2PfjEks4GQ&t=3)
- **PT/INR (Prothrombin time):** Measures how fast blood clots using clotting proteins made in the liver.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXQgjWZCrkhJPViVQcvG3TPKUXFh6fDv31rqP2smICHztDWXUs0zSKgGfmljIy9fEFGUChT6_D1WElnl-PYXepFnzMjPh8Z886_ejkCG0DBL5YS9UmtGGugPlOqYTZ2dbhrMXJ6ASEDZ1eZ6UcCiHp)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESvgEBxCJF1xV8R5RxSgZNKyYKUPMj6_B4npSI0EsjoINqkTGVV-d4PKeYdSBiBI-vKt6vSUEr5xs8RPPK-IUlVO9sFi1i58n-ZGGfwuZ4J-IuTaPBowR2X4X2Hb79Oqc69i-QQ9L7SjzDs40IP7xFacK1ZNy2wXZN-JboikPSb1sJi2K0IMsfmwKf6h0OPa9i4HOomFl0A-YKY6ZWrdeL0yoKZJJKh58zLD-hVEQPLAWAniERkZCE806B2Cq9vIHo)

### Preparation, Risks, and Interpretation

- **Preparation:** Some labs or combined panels require fasting for several hours beforehand, while others have no fasting requirement. Always confirm instructions with your ordering provider or lab.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESowEBxCJF1y_5_YQvrB4OGQRG3CFhgt-HcJxIfQP8KVxww0bWLEGkb7pCR7cNoA6uITVm7xnzBtU0nxyNMllujj5Wnzx3xJqG45EIZVqXTYMuCa4158CGYHLsmkKeFdxtLBf7M0UaJ9-KjWDQG69WLlCGjxpYzaTBwptF9ysc1T0SPnWAbwq8aBHIznr295NW6Kmzt4H5hlETEhstrro3AFQSKM2L)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESngEBxCJF1xM_fzfX-WnVy20M6Fi2B1CvR5dr2J8dCwBDHLycthObt-wr3b9kxJpayj-J8W9qCvtnvVMUYgs4UNAeh6cok2p62WQamaONzBMVJ_nw8ICS4eov8rJhrSprk9SAhtGCqHgQ1hBJ57sQvCi5jWMW3fcP8GqodzxNT_n33eglf1OVMqpsJFenm0eaLkItrM1sMK3JQ1LJ1Le2aA)
- **Risks:** LFTs require a standard blood draw. Risks are low and typically limited to brief discomfort or minor bruising at the needle site.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESngEBxCJF1xM_fzfX-WnVy20M6Fi2B1CvR5dr2J8dCwBDHLycthObt-wr3b9kxJpayj-J8W9qCvtnvVMUYgs4UNAeh6cok2p62WQamaONzBMVJ_nw8ICS4eov8rJhrSprk9SAhtGCqHgQ1hBJ57sQvCi5jWMW3fcP8GqodzxNT_n33eglf1OVMqpsJFenm0eaLkItrM1sMK3JQ1LJ1Le2aA)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXQgjWZCrkhJPViVQcvG3TPKUXFh6fDv31rqP2smICHztDWXUs0zSKgGfmljIy9fEFGUChT6_D1WElnl-PYXepFnzMjPh8Z886_ejkCG0DBL5YS9UmtGGugPlOqYTZ2dbhrMXJ6ASEDZ1eZ6UcCiHp)
- **Interpreting results:** Reference ranges vary slightly by lab, age, and sex. Because non-liver factors—such as medications, alcohol use, muscle strain, or other organs—can affect results, abnormal numbers usually prompt follow-up tests, imaging, or repeat checks rather than a standalone diagnosis.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESagHEIkXXXQu8OiCcKayhN9hSLs9Z10xVOFWsCsktW1jO0wyOvpQFKQbb5WLnghwP3dmTF_aRX6LjAoMbNrfoujix3WrJdk-iM8fAfb-Zhd5MmtWC2p2-YxtECsvmZ0dxnQmYeMIGtvGhVZs)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF1zvHy3I7EcDUXe8Gj6A2DvwxavsXjViDuasQDlHDxVMa4mqR8AQ3F9WQY9luGKtV14i80K4xX6syQpxJXKtH4H7sG3yfCq511khLrtKCc2lMWe9rthJ63-YIoHzQOpocfaHEjtESXyYNPpO1eoTc5SMUGCSbc6AV3U2Ko5fi4IdD4NR_UJIp61swq2I)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXQgjWZCrkhJPViVQcvG3TPKUXFh6fDv31rqP2smICHztDWXUs0zSKgGfmljIy9fEFGUChT6_D1WElnl-PYXepFnzMjPh8Z886_ejkCG0DBL5YS9UmtGGugPlOqYTZ2dbhrMXJ6ASEDZ1eZ6UcCiHp)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiQEBxCJF15xsp2xkEhSIvpzntILRhlsMNltSarB3il487YF-leMKm4wmdRE7ekl20xfJ4SVeerEZogRTQ4H-SKBpGJ-46xvCK0gwIxNz3zYRxQ5CC-ktTQBQjasFj8cKLjVJ6zqms0kglZZAZPnyDkyBIV5y3If7Tq5Dse40mGqIQwc6jv7RrSS7PA)[[5]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESowEBxCJF1y_5_YQvrB4OGQRG3CFhgt-HcJxIfQP8KVxww0bWLEGkb7pCR7cNoA6uITVm7xnzBtU0nxyNMllujj5Wnzx3xJqG45EIZVqXTYMuCa4158CGYHLsmkKeFdxtLBf7M0UaJ9-KjWDQG69WLlCGjxpYzaTBwptF9ysc1T0SPnWAbwq8aBHIznr295NW6Kmzt4H5hlETEhstrro3AFQSKM2L)

items.title: Preparation, Risks, and Interpretation
items.text: Preparation: Some labs or combined panels require fasting for several hours beforehand, while others have no fasting requirement. Always confirm instructions with your ordering provider or lab. Risks: LFTs require a standard blood draw. Risks are low and typically limited to brief discomfort or minor bruising at the needle site. Interpreting results: Reference ranges vary slightly by lab, age, and sex. Because non-liver factors—such as medications, alcohol use, muscle strain, or other organs—can affect results, abnormal numbers usually prompt follow-up tests, imaging, or repeat checks rather than a standalone diagnosis.
